page.title: Triggers
page.purpose: Author a revisit trigger, prove it parses, and dry-run it against current facts before it is saved — so the condition an offer waits on is never a sentence nobody can evaluate.

priorities.statement: Whether this trigger parses, and if not, exactly where it fails
What it evaluates to right now against real facts, before it is saved
Which facts it references that do not exist — the unknown case, distinguished from false
The fact registry and evaluation schedule, ranked below the three above

states.description: The trigger list at rest.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
No triggers are declared yet.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
The declared trigger does not parse. The failing position and what the language admits are both stated; the trigger cannot be saved in this state.
A dry run against current facts evaluates to satisfied, naming each fact and the value that satisfied it.
A dry run evaluates to not satisfied, naming which clause failed and against what value.
A dry run cannot conclude because a referenced fact does not exist. Reported as unknown — never as not satisfied — and the missing fact is named.
Scheduled evaluation has not completed within its interval. Surfaced prominently, because a stalled evaluator silently restores the failure this scenario was built to end.

elements.name: Trigger
elements.description: Where the condition is declared. Admits declared facts, comparison operators and boolean composition — nothing else.
Whether the current declaration parses, updated as it is written rather than only on save.
Where parsing failed and what the language admits at that position. Assertive, because it blocks saving.

elements.name: Dry run
elements.description: Evaluates the declaration against current facts without saving it or producing a proposal.
The result of a dry run: satisfied, not satisfied, or unknown. Three outcomes, never two.

elements.name: Facts used
elements.description: Each fact the declaration referenced and the value it resolved to, so a verdict is explainable rather than asserted.
Names a referenced fact that does not exist in the registry, and how to supply it.

elements.name: Facts
elements.description: The facts a trigger may reference, with their current values and when each was last supplied.
When scheduled evaluation last completed and whether that is within its interval.
Assertive notice that scheduled evaluation has not run within its interval.
Explains what a trigger is and shows a worked example before asking for a first declaration.

claims.statement: A dry run that cannot conclude because a fact is missing is perceivably different from one that concluded not satisfied.
claims.rationale: The scenario's central design rule. Treating unknown as false keeps candidates asleep forever — the exact failure this scenario exists to end — and the UI must not collapse the distinction the evaluator preserves.

claims.statement: An unknown verdict names the fact that is missing and how to supply it.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-005. An unknown verdict with no named cause is unactionable, and the operator's only recourse is guessing which fact to add.

claims.statement: Every dry-run verdict is accompanied by the facts it used and the values they resolved to.
claims.rationale: A trigger the operator cannot check is a trigger the operator will not trust, and an untrusted trigger gets shadowed by a mental reminder — reproducing the original problem.

claims.statement: A declaration that does not parse shows where it failed and cannot be saved.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-003: a node cannot enter or remain in candidate without a machine-evaluable trigger. Accepting an unparseable declaration at the UI puts the invariant back into prose.

claims.statement: The dry-run control and its verdict read before the trigger is committed.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-005 requires triggers to be dry-runnable before being saved. A trigger first evaluated on a schedule fails silently weeks later.

claims.statement: When scheduled evaluation has not completed within its interval, that is stated on this page.
claims.rationale: OBSERVABILITY.md names this the scenario's primary alarm: a dead evaluator is indistinguishable from a quiet one and silently restores the original defect behind a green dashboard.

claims.statement: With no triggers declared, the page explains what a trigger is and shows a worked example rather than an empty editor.
claims.rationale: The trigger language is the one genuinely new concept in the product. An empty text field is the most likely abandonment point.

claims.statement: The dry-run control is operable from the keyboard.
claims.rationale: It sits in an authoring flow that is otherwise entirely keyboard-driven; requiring a pointer here breaks the writing loop.

claims.statement: Each of the three dry-run verdicts carries a text label rather than relying on a status tint.
claims.rationale: PRD accessibility rule, and three outcomes are harder to distinguish by colour than two — the unknown case is the one most likely to be lost.
